s1.syndrome_frame: Acute febrile illness with rash and lymphadenopathy in an immunocompromised host
salient_findings: Painless enlargement of inguinal, axillary, and cervical lymph nodes
key_facts: 43-year-old man
Fever, chills, and headache
Painless ulcer on the prepuce one month prior to admission
Healing of the ulcer prior to development of fever and fatigue
Disseminated maculopapular rash on the trunk and extremities
Multiple unprotected sexual contacts over the past three months
HIV infection diagnosed 10 years ago
Undetectable viral load and CD4 count of 1144 cells/μL
Previous treatment with intravenous penicillin G for suspected otosyphilis
Ill-appearing but not dehydrated on examination
Painless enlargement of inguinal, axillary, and cervical lymph nodes
White-cell count of 63,300/mL with a lymphomonocytic predominance
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis revealed 19 white cells with normal glucose and protein concentrations

shortlist.label: Secondary syphilis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of a painless ulcer on the prepuce, which is a common symptom of primary syphilis, and now presents with a maculopapular rash and lymphadenopathy, consistent with secondary syphilis

shortlist.label: Infectious mononucleosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with fever, headache, and lymphadenopathy, which are common symptoms of infectious mononucleosis, and has a lymphomonocytic predominance on white-cell count

shortlist.label: Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is immunocompromised due to HIV infection and presents with fever, headache, and lymphadenopathy, which are common symptoms of toxoplasmosis

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is immunocompromised due to HIV infection and presents with fever, headache, and lymphadenopathy, which are common symptoms of cytomegalovirus infection

shortlist.label: Lymphogranuloma venereum
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of multiple unprotected sexual contacts and presents with lymphadenopathy and a maculopapular rash, which are common symptoms of lymphogranuloma venereum

raw.rationale: The patient's history of a painless ulcer on the prepuce, followed by a disseminated maculopapular rash and painless lymphadenopathy, is consistent with secondary syphilis, especially given the previous diagnosis and treatment of otosyphilis.

rejected.label: Infectious mononucleosis
rejected.why: Lack of specific symptoms such as sore throat and fatigue out of proportion to other symptoms

rejected.label: Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: No clear exposure history or specific symptoms such as seizures or focal neurological deficits

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus infection
rejected.why: No specific symptoms such as esophagitis or colitis, and the patient's CD4 count is high

rejected.label: Lymphogranuloma venereum
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not include the typical bubo or proctitis seen in LGV
